7. Mr. Karim, therefore, submits that the High Court Division failed to exercise its revisional jurisdiction vested in it by law in failing to consider that the lower appellate Court as a final Court of fact without reversing the aforesaid clear findings of the trial Court pronounced a judgment of reversal and thereby failed to consider that the plaintiff's case being that she tendered the balance consideration of money to the original defendant remains totally uncorroborated and she also failed pay to the further agreed amount as fixed by salish. Mr. Karim further argued that the High Court Division has made out a 3rd case namely, that the provisions for re-conveyance of the suit land on payment of loan money was made after the execution of bainapatra but it was nobody's case since the bainapatra itself came from the custody of the plaintiff-respondent. 

 8. Mr Karim having pointed out that there being no materials on record to show that the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 had ever tried to pay the balance consideration of money as well as the further amount of Taka 10,000 to the original defendant as agreed in Salish, the trial Court having considered all these aspects based on materials on record rightly dismissed the plaintiff's suit with some specific findings and which have not been reversed by the appellate Court without properly controverting the same based on evidence on record and, in such view of the matter, the High Court Division having failed to consider this aspect committed error of law in affirming the judgment of the lower appellate Court and this has not only caused failure of justice but it has seriously prejudiced the appellants. It is a settled principle of law that the lower appellate Court being final court of fact will have to discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the findings of the trial Court. In case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate Court to reassess the evidence on record and to arrive at his own independent finding. In the instant case we find that the specific findings of the trial Court have not been reversed by the lower appellate Court exercising its power under Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
